title: FDA Approves Gefurulimab for Adults With AChR-Positive MG
summary:
Gefurulimab (Klygefa ™) has been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to treat adults with generalized myasthenia gravis (MG) who are positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibodies, AstraZeneca announced.

The treatment, developed by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease, is the first and only dual-binding nanobody C5 inhibitor approved in the United States. It can be self-administered subcutaneously once weekly using an autoinjector.

title: Molecule plus rituximab shows efficacy in membranous nephropathy
summary:
DENVER — A novel molecule plus rituximab was associated with higher response rates vs. rituximab alone, according to study data presented during the high-impact clinical trials session at ASN Kidney Week.

With current B-cell-depleting therapies, significant delays exist between immunologic and clinical responses for patients with membranous nephropathy, according to Brad Rovin, MD, FASN, Lee A. Hebert Professor of Nephrology at Ohio State University.

summary:
A single injection of the lipid nanoparticle encapsulating plasmid DNA coding for factor VIII produced therapeutic levels of factor VIII activity in 2 mouse models of hemophilia A. 

Lipid nanoparticles encapsulating plasmid DNA demonstrated safe, effective, and durable factor VIII expression in preclinical models of hemophilia A, according to a study published in Molecular Therapy.

title: Mouse study maps key brain targets for Dravet gene therapy
summary:
Gene therapy to restore activity of the defective NaV1.1 protein in a specific region of the brain — the hippocampus — is sufficient to reduce seizure risk in Dravet syndrome, according to a mouse study.

title: Genetic 'dimmer switch' can protect against severe disease in rare muscular dystrophy
summary:
Two siblings inherited the same rare genetic disease—a type of muscular dystrophy that progressively weakens the muscles of the face, shoulders and limbs. Although they shared the same disease-causing genetic change, their outcomes were strikingly different. The brother began noticing weakness in his early teens and could barely walk by his 50s. The sister remained symptom-free into her late 30s and was only mildly affected throughout her life.

title: UK Sanfilippo syndrome patients struggle to access $4m therapy
summary:
The BBC recently reported that UK patients with the rare disease mucopolysaccharide (MPS) type IIIa are struggling to access a gene therapy for their condition despite the drug’s approval earlier this year. MPS type IIIa, also known as Sanfilippo syndrome, is a fatal genetic condition that causes neurodegeneration in young children similar to dementia, as well as loss of speech, vision, and mobility. Life expectancy is usually around 15 years.

title: Gazyva Becomes First FDA-Approved Drug for Primary Membranous Nephropathy, a Rare Autoimmune Disease That Attacks the Kidneys
summary:
The Food and Drug Administration has approved Gazyva, or obinutuzumab, for adults with primary membranous nephropathy, the FDA announced Nov. 13. It is the first drug approved specifically to treat adults with the disease, according to the agency.

Until now, doctors have relied on medicines used off-label, including tacrolimus and the CD20-targeting antibody rituximab, sold as Rituxan, Fierce Pharma reported.

title: FDA Grants Orphan Status to Basimglurant, Nerve Pain Pill for Trigeminal Neuralgia
summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted Orphan Drug Designation to basimglurant, an investigational oral drug from Swiss biotech Noema Pharma, for pain associated with trigeminal neuralgia, the company announced Monday. The designation is not an approval, and basimglurant cannot be obtained outside clinical trials.
